quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #7
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: What does this sign show?
questions.correctAnswerText: An intersection.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a road crossing is coming up ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow diamonds with black symbols. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign means a steep hill is coming. Prepare to slow down and drive safely.

questions.question: When you see a drawbridge sign with a flashing yellow light, you should:

options.text: Slow down and get ready to stop.
Stop only if you see a boat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light near a drawbridge means the bridge is opening. Slow down and prepare to stop.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:

options.text: Slow down and drive with care.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Stop and proceed when the way is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and drive with care.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means caution. Slow down, look both ways, and proceed carefully.

questions.question: Bicycles on the road:

options.text: Always must yield to motor vehicles.
Do not have to follow traffic rules.
Are not a concern for drivers.
Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have the same rights and responsibilities as motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on the road. They have the same rights and responsibilities as cars. Drivers must respect bicycle riders.

questions.question: Two solid yellow lines on the road mean:

options.text: Passing is allowed during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines show that traffic is moving toward you. Never cross two solid yellow lines to pass from either direction.

questions.question: The space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
If there is a stop sign.
If you use your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle with sirens or flashing lights approaches, you must right away:

options.text: Pull to the right and stop.
Pull to the right and slow down.
Pull to the right and turn on your flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle uses lights, sirens, or warning devices, drive to the right side of the road and stop right away.

questions.question: Which one must you obey over the other three?
questions.correctAnswerText: A police officer
questions.explanation: A police officer's directions take priority over all signs, signals, and road markings. This includes police officers, fire police, and school crossing guards.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Slow down if an emergency vehicle is near.
Always stop completely at the intersection.
Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: Slow down as you approach a yield sign. Be ready to stop and let other vehicles and pedestrians go first. Stop completely if traffic requires it.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, slow down and pull to the right side of the road. Stop your vehicle to let the emergency vehicle pass. If you are in heavy traffic, move slowly until you have space to pull over safely.

questions.question: You are stranded in a snowstorm. What should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help.
Lay down in your car and go to sleep.
Walk into the road and get the attention of other drivers.
Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the car, as you are most likely to be found when you stay in your vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are easier to find in your vehicle. Walking around outside in a snowstorm is dangerous.

questions.question: When can you safely pass on a two-lane road?

options.text: You are able to clearly see the road ahead.
You can return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.
Your vehicle is capable of the speed necessary to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You can only pass safely on a two-lane road if all three conditions are met: you can clearly see the road ahead, you can return to your lane before oncoming traffic reaches you, and your vehicle can go fast enough to pass. Only pass when it is legal and safe.

questions.question: You are waiting in line at a stop sign. The vehicles ahead have passed through with no cross traffic. What must you do?

options.text: May proceed through the intersection without stopping again.
Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
May slowly roll past the stop sign.
May follow the vehicle directly ahead of you without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
questions.explanation: You must come to a complete stop at the stop sign or stop line every time, regardless of what other vehicles do. Always check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.

questions.question: A police officer is directing traffic at a working traffic light. What should drivers do?

options.text: Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.
Follow the directions given by the officer.
Check to see what the cars next to them are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the officer.
questions.explanation: When a police officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the traffic light. The officer's hand signals control traffic at that moment.

questions.question: A steady yellow traffic light means what color light will appear next?
questions.correctAnswerText: Steady red
questions.explanation: A steady yellow light warns you that a red light is coming next. Prepare to stop.

questions.question: Two vehicles enter an intersection at the same time from different roads. Which vehicle must yield?
questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right. This rule applies to all intersections, whether they have signs, signals, or no controls.

questions.question: You hear a fire engine siren behind you. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a fire engine siren, pull over to the curb or side of the road immediately and stop your vehicle.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and the owner is not there. What must you do?

options.text: May leave the scene without attempting to make contact with the vehicle's owner.
Must contact the vehicle's owner or leave a note.
Must stay near the vehicle until its owner comes to move it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Must contact the vehicle's owner or leave a note.
questions.explanation: If you hit an unattended vehicle, you must try to find the owner and tell them about the accident. If you cannot find them, leave a note with your name, contact information, and license plate number. Also call the police to report the crash.

questions.question: A bus is signaling to return to the main road after stopping. What must you do?

options.text: Honk to let them know you're there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: You must yield to a bus that is signaling to return to the main road. Slow down, change lanes, or stop to give the bus room to safely enter traffic.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers not to enter the road or driveway from your direction. If you see this sign, turn around and take a different route.

questions.question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to drive faster than the train.
Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
Look for a way around any lowered gates.
Assume no trains are nearby and continue driving normally.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossing warning signs warn you that a train may be coming. You must obey these signs and never go around barriers or ignore the warning.

questions.question: What should you do if your accelerator gets stuck while driving?

options.text: Reach down and try to pull it up.
Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal steadily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to neutral and press the brake pedal steadily.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road. Shift into neutral right away and press the brake pedal steadily. When it is safe, pull off the road and turn off the engine.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. When finished turning, your car should be in:

options.text: The right lane of the street.
The left lane of the street.
The lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane of the street.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, complete your turn into the lane closest to the lane you just left.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:

options.text: Drive with your four-way flashers on.
Drive with your parking lights on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights.
questions.explanation: At dusk or on overcast days, you must turn on your headlights. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: What happens to fines for traffic violations in school zones?
questions.correctAnswerText: They are doubled.
questions.explanation: In Florida, fines are doubled for violations in school zones. You may also face civil penalties up to $1,000 and be required to take a driving school course.

questions.question: What should you do on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive the speed limit with caution.
Do not drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down as soon as you see rain, snow, or sleet. These conditions make roads slippery. When road conditions are poor, you may need to drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you drive. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the ignition.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you will need to use more force to steer. Reduce your speed and pull off the road to stop in a safe place.

questions.question: What does this road sign show?

options.text: The maximum safe speed for a residential area.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
The maximum safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The maximum safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum safe speed for exiting a highway. In this example, the safe speed is 30 mph.

questions.question: What does a "No standing" sign mean?

options.text: You can never stop your vehicle there.
You can park there if the driver stays in the vehicle.
You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
You can stop to load or unload goods.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.
questions.explanation: A "No standing" sign means you can only stop briefly to pick up or drop off passengers.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: When it has been raining for an hour or more.
For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
Right after the rain has stopped.

questions.correctAnswerText: For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery in the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain brings oil from the asphalt to the surface. Heat makes this worse by bringing more oil to the road.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane well in advance. Slow down only after you are in the exit lane.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended upward. What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: A left arm and hand extended upward means the driver plans to turn right. Adjust your driving if you are following this vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign alerts you to an upcoming traffic signal. Be ready for a yellow light, red light, or crossing traffic.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, stay farther behind other vehicles. Your car needs more time to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign prohibits U-turns. Do not make a U-turn where this sign is posted.

questions.question: When should you allow extra space in front of your vehicle when stopping?
questions.correctAnswerText: On an incline.
questions.explanation: Allow extra space on an uphill slope. If the vehicle ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, extra space helps prevent a collision.

questions.question: When a funeral procession is present, who has the right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: The funeral procession
questions.explanation: Drivers, pedestrians, and bicyclists must yield to funeral processions. The remaining vehicles in the procession may pass through an intersection after the lead vehicle enters, regardless of traffic signals.

questions.question: If a gate near a drawbridge is about to lower across the road, what should you do?

options.text: Find a way around the gate.
Quickly drive under the lowering gate.
Come to a complete stop and wait for the gate to rise before you proceed.
Stop only if you cannot pass underneath the gate before it lowers completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait for the gate to rise before you proceed.
questions.explanation: Stop when the lights flash and before the gate lowers. Do not drive around or under a crossing gate. It is illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: What color lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: Is driving at night more or less dangerous than driving during the day?
questions.correctAnswerText: More dangerous.
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous than day driving. It is harder to see. Headlights from other cars can blind you. More tired or impaired drivers are on the road at night.

questions.question: What should you do when backing your vehicle?

options.text: Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always look behind your vehicle before backing. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder. What should you do?

options.text: Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.
Stop your car on the edge of the road.
Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
Keep your speed and turn sharply back onto the pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and carefully turn back onto the pavement.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed without braking hard and carefully turn back onto the pavement. Watch for other traffic as you return to the road.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: Stop, then go when the way is clear.
Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You can turn in the direction the arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must stop completely. Wait until a green light or green arrow appears before proceeding, unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to remember about speed on curves?

options.text: Drive the speed limit as you enter the curve, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive the speed limit before, during, and after the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle's momentum can make turning difficult. Slow down before entering a curve to stay in control.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: A lane is ending.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow and black. This sign tells you a lane is ending. Be ready to merge safely.

questions.question: Two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: One driver may go without stopping.
One driver should honk to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a vehicle to your right, let that vehicle go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light mean?

options.text: The same as a stop sign.
You do not have to stop completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Construction work ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency work.
